text: has not shown any survival benefit.2 Prophylactic thyroidectomy may be considered in patients with a hereditary predisposition to medullary cancer.3,8 Resection may relieve symptoms in patients with anaplastic tumours, but cure is impossible and treat- ment is purely palliative, with survival measured in months.3,4,7,9 Neither medullary8 nor anaplastic tumours7 are sensitive to iodine-131. External radiation therapy is commonly used.2,3,9 Chemotherapy has been tried in anaplastic thyroid cancer, as well as in unresponsive disease of other cell types, with limited benefit.2,6 Drugs tried, often in combination regi- mens, include cisplatin, cyclophosphamide, bleomycin, dacarbazine, doxorubicin, fluorouracil, paclitaxel, and vincristine.4,7-9 The vascular targeting agent combretasta- tin A4 phosphate is under investigation.4 1.
